questions.topic: Faithfulness: Is the Answer Grounded in the Context
questions.question: What does faithfulness measure?
options: Whether every claim in the answer is supported by the retrieved context
Whether every claim in the answer is true of the real world right now
Whether the retrieved documents contain the query's own terms verbatim
Whether the answer arrives in the shape and format the user requested

questions.topic: Faithfulness: Is the Answer Grounded in the Context
questions.question: How is a faithfulness score computed?
options: By comparing the answer against the click history for similar queries
By counting the content words shared between the question and answer
By splitting the answer into atomic claims and verifying each in turn
By measuring the embedding distance from the answer back to the query

questions.topic: Faithfulness: Is the Answer Grounded in the Context
questions.question: An answer is perfectly faithful to the retrieved context, yet factually wrong. Where is the defect?
options: In generation, which invented a claim the context never contained
In the citation layer, which pointed at spans that support nothing
In the judge model, which drifted after its version was updated
In retrieval, which supplied context that was itself incorrect

questions.topic: Faithfulness: Is the Answer Grounded in the Context
questions.question: Why is faithfulness computed per claim rather than per answer?
options: One fabricated number in a long fluent answer would be averaged away
Atomic claims are far cheaper to embed than a whole answer would be
Answers cannot be split into sentences reliably enough to be scored
Answer-level scoring needs a gold reference production never carries

questions.topic: Faithfulness: Is the Answer Grounded in the Context
questions.question: A verifier flags `Plan A is cheaper than Plan B` even though both prices are supported in context. What is the right reading?
options: The comparison is fabricated and must be struck from the answer
Context recall is too low, since one of the two prices is missing
Supported inference is legitimate, so the verifier is set too strict
Answer relevance has failed, because no comparison was requested

questions.topic: Context Precision and Context Recall
questions.question: What does context recall measure?
options: The share of the corpus that made it into the index at ingest time
The share of the evidence needed to answer that reached the context
The share of queries that return at least one candidate document
The share of answers that carry at least one citation to a source

questions.topic: Context Precision and Context Recall
questions.question: What does context precision measure?
options: How many chunks each source document was split into at ingest
How quickly the retriever returns its candidates under peak load
How often the index is rebuilt relative to the corpus's churn rate
How many of the chunks sent are useful, and how well they rank

questions.topic: Context Precision and Context Recall
questions.question: Eight chunks are sent to the model and three are relevant. What is the context precision?

questions.topic: Context Precision and Context Recall
questions.question: A relevant chunk sits at position 7 of 10 and the model ignores it. What effect explains this?
options: Models use the start and end of a long context better than the middle
The reranker inverted the ordering, so the strongest chunk ranked last
The chunk fell past the model's token limit and was silently truncated
Embedding similarity decays with a chunk's position in the assembled prompt

questions.topic: Context Precision and Context Recall
questions.question: Why are irrelevant chunks in the context worse than neutral filler?
options: They inflate the storage the vector index keeps for every document
They slow the nightly indexing job that rebuilds the candidate lists
They lower the RRF constant, which flattens the fused ranking scores
They dilute attention and invite plausible but irrelevant material in

questions.topic: Context Precision and Context Recall
questions.question: Context recall is 0.95 but context precision is 0.3, and answers weave in off-topic details. What is the first fix?
options: Raise k so the relevant chunks are certain to be inside the context
Rerank harder and drop chunks that fall below a relevance threshold
Expand every query with HyDE so the candidate pool becomes broader
Re-chunk the corpus larger so each chunk carries more of its context

questions.topic: Answer Relevance and End-to-End Quality
questions.question: What does answer relevance measure?
options: Whether the retrieved context actually contains a usable answer
Whether the answer carries a citation for every claim that it makes
Whether the response addresses the question that was actually asked
Whether the answer reads in the register the brand guidelines set

questions.topic: Answer Relevance and End-to-End Quality
questions.question: A user asks `how do I cancel` and receives a faithful plan comparison. Which metric catches this failure?

questions.question: How does the reverse-consistency check estimate answer relevance?
options: It translates the answer into another language and back again
It asks the user to rephrase the question and then re-runs the whole pipeline
It compares two independent judges' scores to detect a family bias
It writes questions from the answer and compares them to the original

questions.topic: Answer Relevance and End-to-End Quality
questions.question: Why does a correct answer with wrong citations still fail end-to-end review?
options: Citations consume tokens that the generator's output budget needs
Wrong citations destroy trust as effectively as a wrong answer does
Citation errors slow the page render while spans are resolved live
Judges cannot open cited spans, so they score the answer unsupported

The larger sample, because the offline suite covers far more queries
The escalation rate, because online outcomes arbitrate the two
Neither yet, because a moving metric needs a full quarter of data
